newsitem.title: GERMANY: CDU deputy says not backing Waigel's gold plan.
newsitem.headline: CDU deputy says not backing Waigel's gold plan.

text.p: A young member of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) said on Friday he would vote against the government plans to revalue gold and currency reserves to help Germany qualify for European currency union.

CDU deputy Juergen Augustinowitz applauded the German central bank's "single-minded and courageous" stance against Finance Minister Theo Waigel's plans to revalue Bundesbank assets and said he would not to vote for any such legislation.
His comments marked the first cracks in the Kohl government's 12-seat parliamentary majority over the issue.

"I will not take part in any decision in the German Bundestag (lower house of parliament) which would impair the stability of the mark or the independence and credibility of the Bundesbank," he said in a statement.

If Bonn saw its only chance of qualifying for European monetary union in revaluing gold and currency reserves, he said, then it would be better off delaying the launch of Europe's single currency, the euro, planned for 1999.
"If there is no other way round it (filling budgetary gaps) -- then the euro will have to be delayed," he told Reuters in response to an inquiry.

Augustinowitz's remarks came two days after the Bundesbank issued a strongly-worded rejection of Bonn government plans to raise extra cash to plug yawning gaps in the budget by revaluing the central bank assets.
He was the first member of Kohl's CDU/CSU ranks to express his opposition to government plans and take sides with the Bundesbank in the row.
Top leaders in Kohl's coalition have defended Bonn's plan and dismissed calls by the opposition Social Democrats and Greens for Waigel's resignation over the row.

"After the single-minded and courageous stance of the Bundesbank against government plans to revalue currency reserves earlier than planned, I have decided not to vote for a corresponding amendment to Bundesbank law," Augustinowitz said.
